advisories.field: failsIf[30], with failsIf[28] as a second instance
advisories.observation: The successor generalized its anti-collision guard, which is what my v4 finding asked for, but the generalization is narrower than the class it names. failsIf[30] reads 'a basedOn.*.role, whatIsNotAuthored, or failsIf current-standing clause uses a bare version token that collides with this artifact's version integer'. That covers three field families. The defect class is current-standing clauses generally, and the artifact carries at least nine other current-standing prose fields outside that scope: authorityClaim, purpose, registerRowNote, whatIsAuthored, remainderAfterThisCorpus, remeasurementClause, proposedLaterWork, sarifCellStanding and sdkVarianceStanding. A colliding bare token appearing in any of those would trip no guard. Separately, failsIf[28] still enumerates only g20-fixture-corpus.v1 or .v2 as the stale-speaker failure condition for basedOn.g21FixtureCorpusV1.role; since the bump to 4, a stale .v3 or .v4 speaker in that field would trip neither failsIf[28] nor failsIf[30].
advisories.whyNotAFinding: Neither clause is false and neither guarded field is defective right now. failsIf[30] is true as written and the artifact satisfies it: I swept all three named field families, and the six other prose families, and found no bare token colliding with the integer 5. failsIf[28] is true as written, and basedOn.g21FixtureCorpusV1.role does currently carry the correct g20-fixture-corpus.v5 speaker. An under-inclusive guard is a robustness gap in a self-declared failure condition, not an assertion the bytes contradict, and this lineage has graded SHOULD-FIX only where a current-standing clause had a wrong or ambiguous literal reading. Neither has one. Raising this to SHOULD-FIX would also punish the successor for the very generalization it was asked to make.
advisories.whyItStillMatters: The clean sweep at v5 is partly structural rather than earned: no cited artifact sits at version 5, so the bump had nothing to collide with. The next bump does not have that protection. Three cited artifacts sit at version 6 — g20-leftover-join.v6, sdk-leftover-join.v6 and provider-only-nt-gate-join.v6 — and the first two are referred to throughout the artifact by the bare shorthands 'leftover-join.v6' and 'sdk leftover-join.v6', including inside basedOn.leftoverJoinV6.role and basedOn.sdkJoinV6.role, which are exactly the field family failsIf[30] covers. A bump to 6 would therefore recreate the defect at three sites at once, in fields whose current guard would correctly fire.
